beginner.summary: For web developers, identity engineers and administrators new to SAML who need to add SAML 2.0 single sign-on to applications. Covers the roles of Identity and Service Providers, the Web Browser SSO profile, reading assertions, the AuthnRequest and Response protocol, HTTP-Redirect and HTTP-POST bindings, metadata and entity descriptors, NameID formats, attribute mapping, XML signatures, certificates with OpenSSL and xmlsec1, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO, single logout and common errors, using Keycloak, SimpleSAMLphp, python3-saml and SAML-tracer in a safe lab.
prerequisites: Comfortable with HTTP requests, redirects, cookies and browser developer tools
Can read and edit XML and JSON and run commands in a terminal
Has a lab machine with rights to run Keycloak or SimpleSAMLphp, Python with python3-saml, OpenSSL and xmlsec1
outcomes: Explain the SAML roles, message layers and the Web Browser SSO profile
Read, decode and validate SAML assertions, metadata and signatures
Configure a python3-saml service provider against a Keycloak or SimpleSAMLphp IdP
Run SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SSO and single logout, and diagnose common errors

intermediate.summary: For engineers integrating applications with production identity providers. Covers configuring Entra ID, Okta, ADFS, Shibboleth and Keycloak as SAML IdPs, Spring Security SAML and python3-saml service providers, attribute and NameID mapping, assertion encryption, signature validation and trust pinning, the HTTP-Artifact binding, RelayState deep-link handling, just-in-time provisioning, session and logout management, ForceAuthn and AuthnContext including MFA step-up, metadata generation and validation, RSA-SHA256 signing, and mapping groups to application authorization across multiple IdPs.
prerequisites: Completed the beginner level or has run a SAML SSO flow end to end
Has administrative access to at least one IdP such as Keycloak, Okta, Entra ID or ADFS in a test tenant
Can build and run a Python or Spring Boot service provider and edit its SAML settings
outcomes: Configure Entra ID, Okta, ADFS, Shibboleth or Keycloak as a SAML identity provider
Map NameID, attributes, groups and roles reliably between an IdP and an SP
Enable assertion encryption, strict signature validation and SHA-256 signing
Handle sessions, RelayState, just-in-time provisioning, MFA step-up and single logout

advanced.summary: For senior identity engineers running SAML at scale and in federations. Covers certificate and dual-key rollover without downtime, metadata aggregates, per-entity MDQ and automated refresh, the InCommon and eduGAIN federation trust model, security hardening against XML signature wrapping, XXE and replay tested on systems you own, strict audience and recipient validation, single logout across many SPs, attribute release policies and entity categories with GDPR considerations, high availability for IdP and artifact resolution, load testing, auditing and monitoring, CI metadata validation, and migrating from SAML to OpenID Connect.
prerequisites: Completed the intermediate level or operates SAML integrations in production
Comfortable with PKI, XML signatures and reading SAML metadata and assertions in depth
Has a lab with multiple IdP and SP instances and owns the systems used for security testing
outcomes: Execute certificate and key rollover and manage federation metadata at scale
Harden SAML deployments against signature wrapping, XXE and replay on systems you own
Operate single logout, high availability and monitoring across multiple service providers
Plan and run a migration from SAML to OpenID Connect while preserving identity and roles
